City of Pasadena: Municipal government serving about 139,000 residents, with roughly 1,900 full-time employees across 16 departments — including its own water and power utility, public health department, and library system. A full-service city of this size offers unusually broad, stable administrative career paths.
City of South Pasadena: Small city of about 27,000 residents directly south of Pasadena, known as a full-service city that runs its own police, fire, library, water, and recreation departments. City Hall staff is small, so administrative roles tend to touch many departments and offer varied, visible work.
City of San Marino: Residential city of about 12,500 in the San Gabriel Valley that, despite its size, operates its own police, fire, library, and recreation services. Its compact City Hall staff means administrative employees work closely with department heads and the community.
City of Sierra Madre: Foothill town of about 11,000 residents at the base of the San Gabriel Mountains, run as a full-service municipality with 68 full-time employees across eight departments on a roughly $20 million budget. It also operates its own public library, one of the oldest city libraries in Los Angeles County.
City of Glendale: Municipal government of Glendale, a full-service city of about 196,000 just west of Pasadena and one of LA County's largest. It runs its own utility (Glendale Water & Power) plus police, fire, and library systems, so its 1,000-plus-person workforce spans a wide range of stable administrative roles.
City of Burbank: Municipal government of Burbank (pop. about 107,000), the San Fernando Valley city known as the media capital, roughly 15 minutes from Pasadena. A full-service city that operates its own utility, Burbank Water and Power, it offers CalPERS retirement plus a retiree medical trust for employees.
City of Arcadia: Municipal government of Arcadia, a city of about 57,000 directly east of Pasadena in the San Gabriel Valley. It's a full-service, council-manager city running its own police, fire, and library departments — a compact organization where admin staff support core community services with public-sector stability.
City of Monrovia: Municipal government of Monrovia, a foothill city of about 38,000 a few miles east of Pasadena and one of LA County's oldest incorporated cities. It runs its own police, fire, public library, and parks and recreation programs, giving admin staff steady, community-facing work in a small city hall.
City of Alhambra: A full-service city of about 85,000 residents in the San Gabriel Valley, right next to Pasadena, running its own police, fire, library, and parks with roughly 350 full-time staff across 12 departments. A small, stable municipal employer that offers tuition reimbursement and encourages promoting from within.
County of Los Angeles: The nation's largest county government, serving 10 million residents with more than 100,000 employees across 38 departments — from libraries and parks to health and social services. Civil-service hiring means administrative roles exist in nearly every department, with well-established job security and room to move internally.
LA County Department of Mental Health: The largest county mental health department in the U.S., with about 6,000 staff serving over 250,000 Los Angeles County residents a year through clinics and program sites countywide. As an LA County department, admin roles come with civil-service stability and standard county benefits.
LA County Department of Public Health: One of the largest public health departments in the country, protecting the health of LA County's 10 million residents through disease control, immunizations, restaurant inspections, and a network of public health centers. A mission-driven county department where admin staff support programs rather than clinical work, with civil-service stability.
LA County Department of Health Services: Los Angeles County's public healthcare system — the second-largest municipal health system in the U.S. — running four hospitals and more than 20 health centers with over 23,000 staff. Admin roles here are county civil-service positions with pension benefits and strong job stability.
LA County Internal Services Department: The behind-the-scenes LA County department that keeps other county agencies running, handling IT, purchasing, facilities, and a roughly 20,000-vehicle fleet with about 2,200 staff. Steady civil-service work supporting internal county operations rather than serving the public directly.
The Huntington: A private nonprofit research library, art museum, and botanical gardens in San Marino, minutes from Pasadena, drawing about a million visitors a year. Around 500 full- and part-time staff support its collections, education programs, and daily operations.
Descanso Gardens: A 150-acre public botanical garden in La Cañada Flintridge, just west of Pasadena, welcoming over 950,000 visitors a year. It is operated by a nonprofit in a long-running partnership with Los Angeles County, which owns the grounds.
Pasadena Area Community College District: Public community college founded in 1924, serving about 25,000 students across Pasadena and nine surrounding communities as its own single-college district. Classified staff roles come with California public-education stability, pension participation, and set salary schedules.
Glendale Community College: Public, single-college community college district in Glendale, about ten miles from downtown Los Angeles, enrolling roughly 12,000 credit students. Administrative and classified jobs here carry the stability and benefits typical of California public higher education.
Pacific Oaks College: Small private nonprofit college in Pasadena, grown from a Quaker-founded children's school (1945) and known for early childhood education, human development, and marriage and family therapy programs. It operates alongside its on-campus Children's School and belongs to the nonprofit Community Solution Education System.
The Claremont Colleges: TCCS is the nonprofit shared-services organization (established 1925) behind the seven Claremont Colleges, running the central library, campus safety, health services, and business operations for roughly 8,500 students. Its ~300 employees get college-style benefits, including tuition remission and employer-paid retirement contributions.
Norton Simon Museum: Private art museum on Colorado Boulevard in Pasadena holding a renowned collection of more than 12,000 works — European masters plus South and Southeast Asian art — with about 1,000 on view. A small, long-established institution, far more compact and steady-paced than the big LA museums.
